title: Vishal:
headline: Kiva in four lines for someone who has never heard of it: what it does, the idea behind it, how you take part, and Vishal's own closing line.
story: Vishal walks a forest path and explains Kiva in plain words. Four beats, in this order: what Kiva does, the idea behind it (talent is everywhere, opportunity is not), how you take part (you choose the person, as little as $25), and his own closing line.

Kiva approved this story and these bites. The captions follow Brit's CEO-series style: Kiva green, smaller, low, and clear space between letters and between words. “money isn't” must read as two words.
do: Open on frame 1 with Vishal already saying “Kiva helps ordinary people…”, hook text on screen.
Keep the four beats in order. Protect the last line: “So that's Kiva…”.
Small name super from 0:03, after the hook text: “Vishal Ghotge” / “CEO at Kiva”, lower left.
Cover each jump with a short bridge B-roll shot.
End card: “Give a little. Change a lot.” + kiva.org.
dont: Use P1000936 only. An earlier take has the fumble “It's not a loan. It's not a charity.”
No self-intro, no Kiva history, no numbers beyond the $25.
Never “investment” on screen. Write “U.S.”, never “United States”.
No name plate, logo or fade at 0:00. No black first frame.
No crowded captions and no lime: Brit's caption spec only.

transcript:
Seattle shoot 2026, Block 3 Walk and Talk, the final take of “What Kiva actually is”. Times are mm:ss in each file. Names are written as Kiva spells them (the auto transcript writes “Kodke”: it is Ghotge). The camera file and the lav WAV are the same take; the WAV runs about 6.9 s ahead.
--- P1000936.MOV ---
[00:02] Kiva helps ordinary people lend money to individuals around the world who are trying to build a better life for themselves.
[00:10] The concept is simple.
[00:14] Talent and ambition are universal, but opportunity and access to money isn't.
[00:22] And people around the world are working hard and they often lack the resources that are needed for them to succeed.
[00:31] And with Kiva you can help close that gap.
[00:37] When a fisherman is looking to buy a new boat or a farmer is looking to buy seeds,
[00:47] on Kiva you can choose the person you want to support and put as little as $25 and join others who are doing the same.
[00:55] And help this farmer, fisherman, get access to the resources they need so they can grow their own business.
[01:02] And it's simple, when they're done, they repay the money back to you and you can fund somebody else.
[01:08] So that's Kiva, helping connect talent and desire with opportunity.
